keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 382-395: the Goths settled as federates. 'The Goths were given lands inside the Roman Empire itself, in the provinces of Scythia, Mœsia and possibly Macedonia'; they 'served as foederati' and were settled 'under their own authority and were not dispersed'. The page does not say whether the land lay north or south of the Danube and gives no area; Scythia Minor and Lower Moesia are the provinces on the Lower Danube. Drawn: Dobruja plus northern Bulgaria (about 55,000 km2, certainly more than the Goths held), as a federate tint inside Roman land. Macedonia is only 'possibly' named and is not drawn. Infobox area: none on the page.

region.text: 'lands inside the Roman Empire itself, in the provinces of Scythia, Mœsia and possibly Macedonia': Scythia Minor (Dobruja) and Lower Moesia (northern Bulgaria); Macedonia ('possibly') is not drawn

ledger.note: 3 October 382: the Goths are settled in Scythia and Moesia. 'peace was declared on 3 October 382' and 'the Goths were given lands inside the Roman Empire itself, in the provinces of Scythia, Mœsia and possibly Macedonia'. Ricomer and Saturninus negotiated for Rome. The Visigoths page: 'The treaty struck with the Goths was to be the first foedus on imperial Roman soil.' Fritigern, Alatheus and Saphrax 'are never again mentioned in the ancient histories'.

region.text: 'lands inside the Roman Empire itself, in the provinces of Scythia, Mœsia and possibly Macedonia': Scythia Minor (Dobruja) and Lower Moesia (northern Bulgaria); Macedonia ('possibly') is not drawn

ledger.note: 3 October 382: the Goths become Roman federates. 'The Goths recognized the authority of the Roman emperor and were nominally incorporated into the Roman Empire' and 'served as foederati', drafted into the army and, in special cases, 'fielding full armies for Rome'; the Visigoths page: 'semi-autonomous Germanic tribes' bound to 'raise troops for the Roman army' in return for land and legal exemptions. The page does not call them vassals; the dossier follows the burgundian-kingdom model (federates in the lighter tint, empire as counterpart).

region.text: 'lands inside the Roman Empire itself, in the provinces of Scythia, Mœsia and possibly Macedonia': Scythia Minor (Dobruja) and Lower Moesia (northern Bulgaria); Macedonia ('possibly') is not drawn

ledger.note: 395: the federation ends. 'This peace held essentially unbroken until Theodosius died in 395', and in 395 Alaric 'made a bid for the throne' (Visigoths page; the page gives no month for Theodosius's death). The Cliopatria Roman Empire row ends 394 and the Eastern Roman Empire opens 395, so the counterpart string stays 'roman-empire' for the pair.

region.text: 'lands inside the Roman Empire itself, in the provinces of Scythia, Mœsia and possibly Macedonia': Scythia Minor (Dobruja) and Lower Moesia (northern Bulgaria); Macedonia ('possibly') is not drawn

ledger.note: 395: the federate Goths follow Alaric. The visigoths dossier founds the Visigoths in 395, in Thessaly; this dossier's page says only that 'This peace held essentially unbroken until Theodosius died in 395' and that Alaric 'made a bid for the throne'. The Danubian land stays Roman; the Goths move on to Thessaly and Greece (visigoths dossier 395-397).

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-06-a ('Gothic foederati of Moesia and Thrace', 382-395: the 382-395 foederati kingdom has no row anywhere). Three pages opened and two sentences re-read on the Gothic War page; the Thervingi page ends about 378 and has no 382-395 material beyond a chieftain Eriulf who died 391. The Gothic War page names Scythia, Moesia and 'possibly Macedonia', not Thrace; the gothia dossier's hand-over text says 'Scythia (Minor), Moesia and Thrace'. No page opened gives a king or a capital for 382-395 (the Thervingi page says nothing on kingship after 382), so identity.capitals is empty and there is no ruler list. The people are the Thervingi of the gothia dossier plus whatever of the Greuthungi stayed; the visigoths dossier begins in 395 in Thessaly. The Roman Empire row of Cliopatria ends 394, the Eastern Roman Empire starts 395; neither dossier has an event for this federation (roman-empire has no vassal_start 382 for it). Wikidata id unknown.
